utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this: From the very beginning, I never asked for any protective measures. Yesterday, when I came here to this office, I was told that there would be some protective measures put in place. I don't know what they were called. That I would be protected, anyway. And I told you that I do not wish to have protective measures, nor did I ever want protective measures, and that everything that I was going to say would be the truth, and that I don't want to hide behind my own testimony. And then you decided to lift the protective measures which I'd never asked for. And then there was some code name, 009, or some pseudonym or whatever. Some code was assigned initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You continued to be cooperative with the Prosecution until the letter that you sent on -- in May 2008 to us?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I informed you before that, because I had at least 100 telephone calls a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: So on 16 May 2008, you asked to be removed from the witness list?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And that was the first mention that you made of an agreement that you allege with Prime Minister Djindjic that you would never be a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you in 2007, in September, that this agreement existed. I told you, personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, I put it to you that that is a lie. Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me the record of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is there a record of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You never mentioned that man's name in my presence ever before; isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose name, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Djindjic.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tell you that I did. If you have the record, let's look at the record of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, at that meeting you told myself and other representatives of the Prosecution that the Radicals were putting pressure on Prosecution witnesses, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me the record and let me see what I said. I can't remember now. I'm excited and I can't remember what I said. Show me the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And we discussed that you would be the first witness at the trial?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And you said that you were agreeable to testifying, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, certainly, because from the summer -- well, I don't know when the trial started. The telephone kept ringing non-stop. You kept looking for me, looking for me, looking for me. Whether it's true or not, I think it is, and I persistently tried to let you know that I wasn't supposed to come to the trial. I sent medical documentation, I sent you letters, I sent -- I don't know what I didn't send, thinking that there was no need for me to appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And you said you wanted to be a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And in fact, you gave a press interview in October 2008 in which you said you were still a member of the Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. That's a misinterpretation in the daily paper 'Courier,' which has introduced a lot of confusion. I said --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You told the reporter who wrote the story that appeared in 'Courier' that you were still willing to help the party where you could?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was after the conflict between Nikolic and the Radicals.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You said you still had the membership card in your wallet, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I still have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now checking that it can be heard and interpreted into English. That's the main thing. Thank you for testifying, Witness. We are now going to break for 20 minutes, Witness. The court deputy is going to look after you and look after the issue of costs for your day. We are now going to have a 92 ter witness with protective measures, so we'll have to lower the blinds first, and I ask the court deputy to make sure that my mike is repaired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Good afternoon, sir. We are in closed session. You have been granted protective measures. You have been granted a pseudonym, VS-1068. When we move back into open session, your face will be distorted on the screen. Now I'm going to ask you to state your first name, last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I've just been handed is something I have here, but I'd like to draw your attention to the fact that this is not the 92 ter statement, because all the 92 ter statements have that in the title, stating that they're 92 ter statements, and that's what it says in the Prosecution request for witnesses under 92 ter. This is just the 2004 witness statement that I have. I haven't mislaid that, but I don't have the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, this statement we have here was to be admitted pursuant to Rule 92 bis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: 92 ter, yes, Your Honour. There are two statements, two written statements of Witness 1068, dated 18 March, 1995, and 13 June 2004, marked respectively ERN RR04-7394 - RR04-7404, and 0357-8609 - 0357-8616. Your Honours, by the Trial Chamber's second decision dated 27 February 2008, we were granted permission to admit both of these statements to the Court. We were granted under the 92 ter decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm quite so sure, and I don't know why I'm sure about this, but I seem somehow to be sure that you and your fellow Judges will not allow this to be admitted under statement 92 ter. The first statement was given in the Centre of the Security Services of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Mostar. It's a statement taken by the police of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas this statement taken by the Prosecution is not an integral statement, because it follows on to the statement given to the Bosnian authorities or, rather, the Muslim -- authorities of the Muslim-Croatian federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let us check all this. I have here a statement by the witness dated 13th of June, 2004. And you're quite right, there is another statement from the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated 18th of March, 1995, after the first one. So the Prosecutor is requesting the admission of the second statement, the statement of 13th of June, 2004. Madam Prosecutor, is that right? The statement that's to be admitted pursuant to Rule 92 ter is the one dated the 13th of June, 2004?

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are seeking to -- seeking for both the statements to be admitted under 92 ter, as per the DC decision we were allowed. And, Your Honours, for your information, the 13th June 2004 statement is basically the witness basically expanded on the information provided and clarified certain issues discussed in his statement dated 1995, which he gave to the Mostar Security Services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, in the decision of the 27th of February, the Trial Chamber authorised the application of the 92 ter statement for both statements, because the second statement, given to the authorities of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was a supplement to the first statement. So, actually, the 92 ter statement covers both statements, the one dated 23rd of June, 2004, and the one dated 18th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the statement given to the Prosecutor in 2004 is, in fact, a supplement to the statement given to the Muslim authorities in 1995. Now, I'd like to draw attention to the fact that thus far it has never happened that any Trial Chamber of The Hague Tribunal accepts a statement given to the Serbian, Muslim, or Croatian authorities as a statement under 92 ter or 92 bis. Under 92 bis or 92 ter, what was accepted was statements given exclusively to The Hague Tribunal, whereas these two statements, one to the Muslim authorities and one to The Hague Tribunal, is something that the Prosecution is treating as a whole, which is impossible, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good afternoon, Your Honours. It's certainly been the practice of Chambers of the International Tribunal to admit statements, irrespective of to whom those statements were given, as long as the specific terms of Rule 92 ter or 92 bis have been complied with. Mr. Seselj is absolutely wrong when he states that The Hague Tribunal, as he puts it, has never accepted a statement given to the Serbian, Muslim, or Croatian authorities. That is simply not true. The only requirements for the admission of written statements are those that are set forth in the Rule, and there is no specific requirement that a written statement be provided to an investigator of the Tribunal in order for it to be admissible pursuant to Rules 92 bis, 92 ter, or even under Rule 89(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, your submissions have been recorded on the transcript, and I will personally keep that in mind when the Chamber rules on the admission of these statements.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more sentence and I won't interrupt anymore. Mr. President, it was the practice of certain Trial Chambers that statements given to the local authorities were taken under 89(F), because it says there that any statement can be taken under certain conditions. But in practice -- or, rather, the practice to have two statements treated as one statement under 92 ter is something that I am not aware of. So Mr. Mundis can tell me which Trial Chamber accepted something like that and when. Here we have two quite separate statements, and the Prosecution is treating them as one statement under 92 ter, whereas in other cases the Prosecution prepares special 92 ter witnesses, and if the witness gave more than one statement, then they make a compilation of all those statements and provide one text, whereas here you, in fact, have two statements, and there are contradictions in those two statements. Unfortunately, I'm not able to point out those contradictions, because as you know, a priori, I refuse to accept that type of testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will rule on the matter in due course. I'm not aware of this practice. It's a first for me. The Trial Chamber will rule on this. Ms. Prasad, we are in open session. Please give us the summary of these two statements, since we are talking about two statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But can you read the first part in open session, and then we should move into private session. Okay, so when the time comes, please ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The witness is a Bosniak Muslim. In 1992, he was 21 years old when the events unfolded in Mostar. On 3rd April 1992, there was a tank explosion near the Northern Camp in Zalik, Mostar. As a result, around 500 to 600 people, including Serbs, Croats and Muslims, took refuge in a shelter in Zalik, as they felt safer there. In May 1992, the Serbs took over the area and restricted the movement of all non-Serbs. On 7th May, few reservist troops entered the shelter and selected ten non-Serbs and took them away. The when they were brought back, the detainees informed the rest that they were taken to Northern Camp barracks, where they were forced to kneel with their heads bowed down the entire night. Around 13 May 1992, a Chetnik entered the shelter and announced that more Chetniks were advancing and he was about to begin cleansing Bijelo Polje. On 22nd May 1992, a Chetnik police commander from Zalik came to the shelter and made a list of people who would clean the city and the ruins. The detainees were labour to clean streets and garbage at locations where shooting and shelling was ongoing, endangering their lives, and using them as human shields. On 13 June 1992, having heard that the Northern Camp would be mined, the witness and several hundred people gathered at the shelter, but the number of people kept increasing as Chetniks were forcing them out of their apartments and bringing them to the shelter. A few Chetniks came to the shelter and demanded that all male detainees line up outside with their ID cards. Then they were taken to Northern Camp barracks. From there, the witness, along with 15 other detainees, was transported in a truck to a town cemetery building. They were imprisoned in a room and taken one by one for interrogation. They could hear moans and cries for help. Most of the detainees, including the witness's father, never returned. The witness was also taken for interrogation, during which he was beaten and a knife was held to his throat, and a loaded gun to his head, and one of the interrogators threatened him to answer or he would pick his eyes out and cut off his ears and throat. After 20 minutes, the witness was thrown into a dark room full of interrogated people. Your Honour, at this point can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, I would like to proceed with questions regarding the statement to the witness. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Witness, did you give a statement on 18 March 1995 to the Ministry of Interior, Mostar Security Services?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: And then on 13 June 2004, when you met with the representatives of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review your written statement in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked through my statement, yes, in my own language.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Usher, could you please display a hard copy of the B/C/S version of the statement dated 18 March 1995, and we can hand a copy to the witness, bearing 65 ter number 5035B. And, please, it's not to be broadcasted, the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the first page of the B/C/S statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wanted to check if he has the 1995 statement, dated 18 March 1995. Are we -- we have to give him the 1995 -- 18th March 1995. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the first page of the statement. Do you recognise your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Please flip through the pages and look at page 11 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Now, Usher, can you please hand out the hard copy of the English and the B/C/S version of the statement dated 13 June 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise your signature on the first page of the English version?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Can you flip through the pages and turn to page 7?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to bring to your attention that the B/C/S version of the 13 June 2004 statement was signed by the witness subsequently in November 2004, bearing ERN 0363-1619 - 0363-1627. This range is different from the ERN range that was granted pursuant to the DC decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Witness, do these statements together accurately reflect your recollection of the events described in it?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they accurately reflect what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: And if you were asked questions about those events today, would you give the same answers that are contained in the statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEKSANDER STEFANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would move for the admission, under seal, of the two written statements of the witness, dated 18 March 1995 and 13 June 2004, bearing 65 ter number 5035B and 5035A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to give two MFI numbers, because the trier will have to hand down a decision as to the final tendering into evidence. Two MFI numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P658 and P659, both MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under seal?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... statement will become Exhibit P658 and the 2004 statement will become Exhibit P659, both marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. But remember that it should be under seal, because this is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have to keep everything in mind. Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PRASAD
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission, I would like to ask the witness two questions in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of November, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 24 25
